# 說無垢稱經

**Category:** 經集部類

**Dynasty:** 唐
**Date:** 650
**Juans:** 6

## Contributors

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Shuō wúgòuchēng jīng* (T476) is Xuánzàng's 玄奘 ([玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98)) six-fascicle translation of the *Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa-sūtra*, produced in 650 CE shortly after his return from India. Xuánzàng renames the protagonist *Wúgòuchēng* 無垢稱 ("Spotless Renown") — a more literal Chinese rendering of *Vimalakīrti* (Sanskrit *vimala* = pure, *kīrti* = renown) — replacing the older transliteration *Wéimójié* used by Zhī Qiān ([KR6i0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0075)) and Kumārajīva ([KR6i0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0076)). The Taishō header cross-references Nos. 474 and 475.

**Abstract**

Xuánzàng's translation represents the third and most literal Chinese rendering of the *Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa-sūtra*. Working from a Sanskrit *Vorlage* he had brought back from India, Xuánzàng produced a longer (six-fascicle) and more philosophically precise text than Kumārajīva's polished three-fascicle classical version. Xuánzàng's renderings of technical terms reflect his Yogācāra training — *upāya*, *bodhi*, *nirvāṇa*, etc. are translated according to the Cí'ēn 慈恩 school's standardized terminology. The translation date of 650 CE places it among Xuánzàng's earliest post-return translations (he returned in 645 CE).

Despite Xuánzàng's translation being more accurate to the Sanskrit, Kumārajīva's [KR6i0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0076) version retained its cultural primacy in East Asian Buddhism. Xuánzàng's version was studied primarily within the Cí'ēn (Yogācāra) school. [窺基](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AA%BA%E5%9F%BA) Kuījī's *Shuō wúgòuchēng jīng shū* ([KR6i0085](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0085) = T1782) is the principal Yogācāra commentary on this version.
